title: Notification
description: What a producer tells a reviewer surface about a Docket entry that nobody asked it about: a deadline approaching, a deadline passed, a state change (INVARIANTS.md DK-1, DK-3). One discriminated union with a `kind` property, added in v0.1 — the seed's two notifications were told apart by which properties they carried, and a consumer switching on the presence of fields is exactly what AF-5 forbids. A notification is a HINT, never a fact a consumer may act on alone: expiry is queryable state, so an entry past its deadline reads expired whether or not any sweep has run or any notification arrived.

docketExpiring.title: DocketExpiringNotification
docketExpiring.description: A pending entry is approaching its deadline. RE-SENT on every sweep while the entry stays inside the warning window, so a consumer must treat repeats for the same docketId as idempotent — key a countdown off expiresAt rather than counting notifications.

expiresAt.description: When the entry expires. The boundary is inclusive.

docketExpired.title: DocketExpiredNotification
docketExpired.description: A pending entry lapsed without a reviewer decision. The write it carried is not committed. A decision arriving after this is refused, and — when it came from a principal who could have decided — its amendments are preserved on the row for a resubmission (DK-1).

docketTransition.title: DocketTransitionNotification
docketTransition.description: An entry changed state (DK-1). New in v0.1, and the shape of the docket.transition telemetry event the registry names (TL-1): the state it left, the state it reached, and the execution outcome an approved row now carries.

execution.description: The execution outcome the row now carries, or null when it is not approved.
